measurement_policy.rule: Image generation may change registered surface appearance only; it may not determine geometry, placement, roof topology, or openings.

source_backed_facts.fact: A large two-story gambrel barn with lower shed portions.
The construction is described by HABS as a gambrel-with-shed log barn.
HABS records the barn approximately 135 feet northeast of the house.

must_preserve_at_all_lods: gambrel break on both main roof slopes

surface_family.walls: weathered horizontal logs with restrained chinking
surface_family.gable_and_doors: weathered vertical or framed timber as confirmed by HABS elevations
surface_family.roof: weathered timber/shingle field as confirmed by close reference
surface_family.foundation: derive from HABS drawing and current photographs; do not invent a continuous exposed plinth

openings.rule: Use WY-152-C measured elevations and exterior photographs; do not copy the T. A. Moulton opening pattern.

structures.name: John and Bartha Moulton Residence (Pink House)

source_backed_facts.fact: A 1.5-story frame residence finished in pink-tinted stucco.
The current NPS place page describes the house as built around 1934; the HABS parent record and a 2021 NPS preservation release describe it as circa 1938.
source_backed_facts.note: Retain the date discrepancy as provenance; it does not authorize geometry interpolation.

source_backed_facts.fact: HABS locates the house approximately 70 feet west of Mormon Row Road and 300 feet north of Antelope Flats Road.
NPS historic-condition reporting describes bright green doors and windows.

massing.primary_roof: extract exact topology from HABS WY-152-A plans and elevations
must_preserve_at_all_lods: relationship of main body and documented additions

surface_family.walls: muted salmon/pink stucco; avoid modern saturated pink
surface_family.trim: historically supported green doors and window trim, calibrated from rights-cleared current references
surface_family.roof: derive material and colour from HABS/current same-building references
surface_family.foundation: derive from HABS and post-stabilization references; do not reproduce temporary preservation works

openings.rule: Use WY-152-A plans/elevations for count and placement; projection may add surface detail but not change openings.

structures.name: John Moulton Homestead Minor Buildings and Corral

source_backed_facts.fact: The HABS parent record lists two outhouses, a shower house, bunkhouse, granary, pumphouse, and corral among the extant homestead features.
Fences, corrals, irrigation features, cleared fields, and pasturage are significant parts of the Mormon Row cultural landscape.

generation_policy.buildings: Use shared low-cost timber and roof materials; create only structures whose identity and footprint can be resolved from HABS/site evidence.
generation_policy.context: Represent corrals, fences, and irrigation through existing prop/setting systems when available, not as baked building geometry.
generation_policy.fallback: Omit an unresolved minor component rather than invent its position or form.

unresolved_before_generation: Resolve unique barn and house footprints and orientations against the present geospatial data.
Determine which minor-building footprints can be identified without speculation.
Confirm current roof and foundation materials from item-level, rights-cleared references.
Reconcile historic versus post-stabilization house foundation appearance for the target presentation date.
